task.description: WF-02, step 1b — gate CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR on the design of REQ-105 (docs/design/REQ-105-e2e-picker.md). Read the design and the block REQ-105 yourself, not the summary of the author, and check by the section "Step 1b" of docs/workflows/WF-02-development.md: every one of the ten criteria leads to an element of the design and to a test; signatures, data and errors are complete (the starter stand.js, its fixture stand-in, the spec); the bar section Q1-Q14 and R1-R3 is complete; protection stands in the same operation as the action; no contradiction with decisions/ (0107, 0108, 0109, 0023); no implementation code; the statements about the current system are repeated BY YOU on a fresh clone of the tag base/E2E105-20261105-01 (git clone -b, outside the project; the design file and decision 0109 are new files and are not in the tag, read them from the working folder); run the earlier tests after the replacement table (E2K-50, E2K-41, E2K-60 and the whole kit test file) with the new dummy files; apply at least 10 mutants of the design yourself (the product mutants against the real picker page and the real server, not only the design's list) and report each with the test that catches it or the gap; measure the time budget claim (section 7) yourself, three runs, and say how far it is from the 80000 ms limit; assess the size and order of the sub-steps (section 14); check the order check on two real files (section 13). Two points to judge with your own measurement: O3 (start button below the window at 320x568 in Russian — is it a page defect that the requirement forbids to hide, or a scrolled page?) and O4 (the declared network error line, exactly two entries). Any item not passed is a FAIL, there is no partial credit. Task text and your report hold no absolute machine paths and no names of other projects of the owner.

summary.O3: Judged by my own measurement (tenants uchet-pro and svet-marketing, ru, kk, en, windows 1470x784, 390x844, 320x568): the start button lies fully inside the window in 7 of the 9 language-window pairs of each tenant (identical for both tenants); at 320x568 in Russian AND Kazakh (not only Russian, as the design says) it lies at 546..594 (bottom 26 px below the 568 edge) and in English at 495..543 (inside). The document there is 643 px high, html and body have overflow visible, no element is position:fixed, the page scrolls normally, window.scrollTo(0,0) then scrollIntoView puts the whole button at 520..568 inside the window; horizontal: left 29, right 291 of 320, scrollWidth equals innerWidth. REQ-057 promises at 320x568 only 'no horizontal scroll' and controls of at least 44x44 (the button is 262x48); it does not promise the button on the first screen. Verdict: a scrolled page, not a page defect; the design's reading (horizontal containment plus the whole rectangle inside the window after scrollIntoView) is right and is not a weakening, because the vertical reading is checked in the only form the page promises (reachability).
summary.O4: Judged by my own measurement (six runs of the lost-net scenario, two with 3 s waits before and after the stop): every run gave exactly three console entries - the favicon 404 line once and exactly two `Failed to load resource: net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` with url .../t/uchet-pro/api/result?lang=ru (one per press, two POST records), focus on the retry button, stop code 0, no exception entry. Deterministic, so the declaration by exact text with path plus 'exactly two' is a sound, not a weakened, reading of 'the kit reports none'. The residual risk (the freed port reused by another process during the test) is theoretical and not a remark.

findings.pass_item: B6, C8 (and Q3: an oracle not run)
findings.place: section 8, row of criterion 5 ('no `@`, no run of 7 digits in the text of the value')
findings.what: The value of `sai-picker:uchet-pro` holds the field `version`, the 64-hex hash of the questionnaire. For uchet-pro it is d4f0885bf5b34469014bcd2e57258ddc04056c5bdf661363749a035ab5a55ee8 and contains the run `3446901` (seven digits). I wrote the assertion as the text says (on the whole stored text) in my extended spec: `storage` is red with 'The expression evaluated to a falsy value' on the correct page, deterministically (the hash is fixed by the tenant file). A hex string of 64 characters contains a run of 7 decimal digits with a high probability, so any tenant version can trip it. The prototype has no such assertion, so the designer never ran it. With the version cut out of the text first the assertion holds (my run).
findings.needed: Name what the 'no free text / no contact data' check is applied to (the `answers` and `current` and `lang` parts, not `version`), or drop the digit rule and keep the check on the keys and on '@'; say which. Re-run the final assertion on the prototype.

findings.place: section 11.1, E2S-05 ('the `env` event of the stand-in lists only names from the base list, the given ones and its own two variables')
findings.what: On macOS every Node child receives `__CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING` from the system whatever environment the parent passes: `env -i PATH=... node -e 'console.log(Object.keys(process.env))'` prints `[ 'PATH', '__CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING' ]`, and a spawn with env {PATH, TMPDIR} gives `PATH, TMPDIR, __CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING`. My starter check built from the text of E2S-05 is red on the developer's machine for exactly this name (the starter itself is right). The test as worded is red on the owner's Mac.
findings.needed: E2S-05 must assert what matters (no name that is not in the base list, the given list or the stand-in's two variables, apart from a named allowance for names the operating system adds on its own, or: the four named leak names are absent and the given names are present). Say which, and name the allowance.

findings.pass_item: A3 (sub-step order and the expected red tests)
findings.place: section 14, sub-step 3 against section 12 row 1 ('SCANNED gets tools/test/e2e/picker.e2e.js')
findings.what: Sub-step 3 (TEST-DESIGNER) edits E2K-50 so that SCANNED lists `tools/test/e2e/picker.e2e.js`, but the file is created only in sub-step 4a. E2K-50 reads every listed file with readFileSync: with the edit and without the file it fails with ENOENT (measured in my clone: `node --test --test-name-pattern=E2K-50 test/e2e-kit.test.js` -> not ok, ENOENT picker.e2e.js). The design says 'none red after it; `node --test test/e2e-stand.test.js test/e2e-kit.test.js` -> exit 0'. That check is red until 4a.
findings.needed: Move the SCANNED entry to sub-step 4a (with the spec), or state the red test after sub-step 3 as EXPECTED_RED with the reason; correct the expectation of the sub-step table and of section 9 accordingly.

findings.place: section 16, S02; section 4.3 mode `with-child`; section 11.1 E2S-13
findings.what: S02 (no SIGKILL to the group after the main process ended) survives E2S-13 as described: the stop sends SIGTERM to the whole group and the sleeping child of the stand-in dies from that signal, so the final SIGKILL never has anything to do. In my run S02 was red nowhere (the other 15 starter mutants I applied were red where the design says).
findings.needed: Say in 4.3 that the child of `with-child` ignores SIGTERM (only SIGKILL removes it), and that E2S-13 checks it is gone.

findings.place: section 16, P21 ('the page sends an answer of a hidden question' -> caught by `pass`)
findings.what: Applied by me (bodyAnswers returns the raw answers): survives. In a pass that never answers a question that later becomes hidden, the raw and the pruned answers are equal, so the request body is equal in both. The claim 'caught by pass (request body deep-equal)' does not hold for the planned passes.
findings.needed: Either add to `pass` one path that answers, goes back, changes the answer that hides a question and presses on (and compare the body), or mark P21 as not caught here (REQ-057's own test guards it).

findings.what: R07 (hasStack with `\s`) is said to be caught by E2S-20, but the described negative case is 'a text with `at ` inside a line'. Checked in node: `we arrive at the end` is false for both the right and the mutated expression; only a text with an empty line followed by a line that starts with `at ` (`note\n\nat start`) separates them.
findings.needed: Name that negative case in E2S-20.

findings.place: section 16 (the check after the series: `pgrep -f 'sai-e2e-'`), section 1 F30
findings.what: A leaked stand is a plain `node src/picker/cli.js serve ...` or `node .../fake-stand.js` whose command line has no `sai-e2e-`; the pgrep cannot see it. Proof: when I came, two picker servers (started 00:26 local) from the designer's sketches were still alive with the designer's scratch folder as their folder, after F30 said nothing was left; my own S07/S08/S09/S16/S20 mutants leaked 20 stand-in processes the same way, which that command would not have listed (I killed mine by pid).
findings.needed: The after-series check must list processes by the program that was started (`cli.js serve`, `fake-stand.js`) or by their working folder, not only by `sai-e2e-`; add it to section 16 and to E2S/RV commands.

findings.what: When the program cannot start (bad cwd) the child has no pid and the error comes as an event. The text does not say what steps 4 and 7 do with an undefined pid. In the sketch (guard on pid, then `waitGroupGone(undefined, 3000)`) the call takes 3025 ms for nothing before STAND_START_FAILED is thrown (measured).
findings.needed: One sentence: with no pid, nothing is registered, signalled or waited for; the marker is removed and the error thrown at once.

findings.what: My mutant Q16 (the dark block applies only to windows of 400 px and wider, so at 390 and 320 the dark scheme shows the light colours) survives the whole spec: `themes` reads colours in one window only and `matrix` sets the scheme per combination but asserts no colour. The requirement as written does not ask more, so this is not a blocking gap, but the matrix says 'each of the two colour schemes'.
findings.needed: Optional and cheap: in `matrix` also read `matchMedia(dark)` and the body background per combination (different between the two schemes in each window).

findings.place: section 1 F8 and section 19 O3 ('at 320x568 in Russian')
findings.what: Kazakh has the same position (546..594) in both tenants; English fits. The assertion is generic, so no test changes, but the text names Russian only.

If the process ended with a bad code and the group is still alive after the SIGKILL wait, both CLEANUP_FAILED and STAND_EXIT apply; the text lists CLEANUP_FAILED first in one sentence and STAND_EXIT after it without a rule. `noisy` ends 'with the line END': on one stream or on both is not said, E2S-12 says both streams end with END.
findings.needed: State which error wins and that both streams end with END.

issues.text: Facts of the task checked: the tag base/E2E105-20261105-01 exists (4f41032); the block has ten criteria (the task says ten); decision 0109 and the design are new files not in the tag. The task names no expected verdict (AP-018 not applicable). Task asks me to set started_at; the protocol lets only ORCH write it, and it was already set at 2026-11-04T20:04:38Z, so I left it.

For ORCH: two picker servers (pid 17526 and 17610, started 00:26 and 00:26 local on 2026-11-05, working folder inside the designer's scratch clone) are still alive, parent pid 1. They are not mine and I did not kill them; they are leftovers of the designer's sketches (see N7). Eight old `node -e setInterval(...)` processes (pids 10044 .. 14481, with spaces in the text) are also not mine and were left.

Rework route: FAIL goes back to CODE-DESIGNER with N1-N3 (blocking, Medium) and N4-N11 (Low, fix in the same pass if cheap). Nothing else needs redesign. O2, O3, O4 of decision 0109 are confirmed by my measurements; O3's wording and N10 go to DOC-UPDATER at step 10 as in section 17.

For docs/anti-patterns.md candidates (Q13), from this gate: an oracle written in a design and not run on the prototype can be false on the real data (hex hash contains digit runs); a test of the environment of a child must allow names the operating system adds; adding a path to a scan list one step before the file exists leaves a red test; a leak check by a name that the leaked process does not carry sees nothing.
